subject: biology
title: Speciation, Extinction & Lamarck
welcome_lead: Time to stretch — see how isolated populations split into new species, why mass extinctions reset life, and where Lamarck went wrong.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology stretch — speciation by isolation, 5 mass extinctions, Darwin vs Lamarck, reading evolutionary trees.
final_note: You learned how isolation + selection makes new species, the 5 mass extinctions, why Lamarck's 'inherited use' was wrong, and how to read evolutionary trees.

concepts.def: Formation of a new species from an old one
Populations split by mountains, rivers or oceans
When the last member of a species dies out
Sudden loss of many species worldwide (5 so far)
Claimed acquired traits in life were inherited
Diagram showing how species share ancestors

walkthroughs.body_html:
Step 1: A population is split — a river, a mountain, an island.

Step 2: Each side faces different selection pressures.

Step 3: After enough generations, the two groups can't interbreed. New species!

Earth has had 5 mass extinctions — the most famous wiped out non-bird dinosaurs ~66 million years ago.

Causes: asteroid impact, volcanic eruptions, climate change, sea-level shifts.

Many scientists warn a 6th is underway — driven by humans.

Lamarck: a giraffe stretches its neck → longer neck → passed on. WRONG — body changes during life aren't inherited.

Darwin: giraffes vary in neck length → long-necked ones reach more food → survive → reproduce → pass on the alleles. Correct.
